title: Manish Gulati v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Tarun Agarwala and Pramod Kumar Srivastava, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; representation treated as Clause 6.5 application; disconnection stayed.
headnote: Pending representation against alleged inflated bills treated as a Clause 6.5 application; Executive Engineer directed to decide by a speaking order within four weeks; coercive disconnection stayed for six weeks or until that disposal, whichever is earlier.
facts: Manish Gulati petitioned the Allahabad High Court alleging that Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited had issued inflated electricity bills. His representation against those bills remained pending, while the licensee proceeded with coercive disconnection. Without examining the bills on merits, the Division Bench disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer to treat the representation as a Clause 6.5 application and decide it by a speaking order, staying disconnection for six weeks or until that disposal, whichever was earlier.

holding_units.topic: pending representation treated as Clause 6.5 application
holding_units.holding: A consumer representation against alleged inflated bills, left undecided while disconnection is threatened, is to be treated by the Executive Engineer as an application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and decided by a reasoned speaking order; coercive disconnection remains in abeyance for six weeks or until that disposal, whichever is earlier.

not_decided.point: Whether the electricity bills were inflated
not_decided.note: Writ disposed without examining the billing dispute on merits; relegated to Clause 6.5.
